raw_source_fields.traits: Heritable information; metabolism; evolutionary descent
raw_source_fields.note: All known cellular organisms share ancestral biochemical systems. Oldest evidence of life is debated, with multiple geochemical and stromatolite lines of evidence.

raw_source_fields.traits: Prokaryotic organization; diverse cell envelopes; extraordinary metabolic breadth
raw_source_fields.note: Bacteria are one of three major cellular domains; metabolism reshaped Earth long before animal life.

raw_source_fields.traits: Distinct membrane lipids; archaeal information processing; diverse chemistries
raw_source_fields.note: Archaea include methanogens, salt-tolerant groups and lineages closely related to eukaryotes. Deep branching remains actively revised.

raw_source_fields.traits: Nucleus; endomembranes; mitochondria or descendants; cytoskeleton
raw_source_fields.note: Eukaryotic cellular complexity arose through symbiogenesis and gene exchange; multicellularity arose independently several times.

raw_source_fields.count: Tens of thousands formally named species
raw_source_fields.traits: Bacterial ribosomes; varied respiration and photosynthesis; rapid horizontal gene transfer
raw_source_fields.note: Bacterial metabolisms include oxygenic photosynthesis, nitrogen fixation, sulfate reduction, and aerobic respiration.

raw_source_fields.traits: Ether-linked membrane lipids in many; archaea-specific molecular machineries; methanogenesis in some
raw_source_fields.note: Archaea occupy terrestrial, marine, host-associated, and high-temperature habitats, not only extremes.

records.common_name: Animals, fungi, and their protist relatives

raw_source_fields.common: Animals, fungi, and their protist relatives
raw_source_fields.traits: Ancestral single posterior flagellum; shared molecular synapomorphies
raw_source_fields.note: This evolutionary branch includes animal and fungal ancestors, with important single-celled relatives not fully shown in the atlas.

raw_source_fields.traits: Primary plastids derived from cyanobacteria; photosynthetic lineages
raw_source_fields.note: Primary plastid endosymbiosis enabled the evolution of red algae, green plants, and glaucophytes.

raw_source_fields.traits: Plastids; cellulose-rich cell walls; photosynthesis; alternating generations in land plants
raw_source_fields.note: Green plant ancestry lies among freshwater-related green algal lines; land colonization reshaped soils, weathering, and atmospheric carbon. Circumscription of Plantae varies.

raw_source_fields.traits: Absorptive nutrition; chitin-rich walls in many; hyphal networks common
raw_source_fields.note: Fungi evolved potent extracellular digestion, mineral uptake and symbioses; mycorrhizal partnerships aided land plants.

raw_source_fields.traits: Many with complex plastids; diverse flagella; marine primary production
raw_source_fields.note: Chromista is a classification-dependent assemblage. Its boundaries and monophyly are debated; many lineages arose through complex plastid symbiosis.

raw_source_fields.traits: Mostly unicellular eukaryotes; phagocytosis in many; diverse motility
raw_source_fields.note: Traditional Protozoa is paraphyletic: organisms grouped under it do not form one exclusive evolutionary branch. Shown as a historical taxonomic category.

raw_source_fields.traits: Oxygenic photosynthesis; chlorophyll a; thylakoids in many
raw_source_fields.note: Cyanobacterial oxygen production helped drive the Great Oxidation Event; a cyanobacterium became the ancestor of plastids.

raw_source_fields.traits: Heterocysts in many; nitrogen fixation; filaments
raw_source_fields.note: Some members specialize cells to fix nitrogen while neighboring cells produce oxygen.

raw_source_fields.ety: Traditional name applied to gelatinous colonies
raw_source_fields.traits: Gelatinous colonies; heterocysts in many
raw_source_fields.note: Nostoc species inhabit soils, rock surfaces and freshwater, often responding to periodic wetting.

raw_source_fields.traits: Nitrogen-fixing colonies; desiccation tolerance
raw_source_fields.note: Visible gelatinous colonies expand rapidly after rain.

raw_source_fields.traits: Diverse Gram-negative lineages; photosynthesis or heterotrophy
raw_source_fields.note: Includes many symbionts, marine bacteria, soil organisms and pathogens.

raw_source_fields.traits: Highly varied respiratory and ecological strategies
raw_source_fields.note: Includes enteric bacteria, vibrios, and many marine groups.

raw_source_fields.traits: Facultative anaerobes common
raw_source_fields.note: Includes abundant gut-associated and environmental species.

raw_source_fields.traits: Gram-negative rods; fermentative capacity in many
raw_source_fields.note: Contains model organisms and pathogenic relatives.

raw_source_fields.traits: Facultatively anaerobic enteric organisms
raw_source_fields.note: E. coli became a central model for molecular genetics and microbial ecology.

raw_source_fields.traits: Enormous strain diversity; adaptable metabolism
raw_source_fields.note: Most strains inhabit vertebrate guts without causing disease, while certain lineages are pathogenic.

raw_source_fields.traits: Many Gram-positive lineages; spore formation in some
raw_source_fields.note: Important decomposers, gut symbionts, fermenters, and pathogens.

raw_source_fields.traits: Some form endospores
raw_source_fields.note: Contains Bacillus and relatives adapted to contrasting habitats.

raw_source_fields.traits: Aerobic and facultative taxa; endospores in some
raw_source_fields.note: Includes soil-adapted bacterial lineages.

raw_source_fields.traits: Bacterial spores in many members
raw_source_fields.note: Common in soils and other terrestrial habitats.

raw_source_fields.traits: Resistant endospores
raw_source_fields.note: Includes widely studied soil microorganisms.

raw_source_fields.traits: Sporulation; biofilm formation; competence
raw_source_fields.note: A classic bacterium for studying cellular differentiation and gene regulation.

raw_source_fields.traits: Methanogenesis in several lineages; halophiles
raw_source_fields.note: Traditional Euryarchaeota membership is heavily revised in newer phylogenomic systems.

raw_source_fields.traits: Methanogenesis; hydrogen metabolism
raw_source_fields.note: Methane production is an ancient biological source of atmospheric methane.

raw_source_fields.traits: Hydrogenotrophic methane production common
raw_source_fields.note: Grow in anaerobic environments, including animal digestive systems.

raw_source_fields.traits: Methane-producing metabolism
raw_source_fields.note: A group involved in anoxic carbon cycling.

raw_source_fields.traits: Often host-associated
raw_source_fields.note: Some species inhabit mammal intestines.

raw_source_fields.traits: Hydrogen-consuming methanogenesis
raw_source_fields.note: Common archaeal member of human gut microbiomes.

raw_source_fields.traits: Many heat-adapted members; archaeal cell biology
raw_source_fields.note: Contains branches formerly placed within Crenarchaeota; broader modern usage varies.

raw_source_fields.traits: Acidothermal adaptations in many
raw_source_fields.note: Diverse archaea thrive in sulfur-rich hot springs.

raw_source_fields.traits: Thermoacidophily common
raw_source_fields.note: Oxidize sulfur compounds in acidic thermal environments.

raw_source_fields.traits: Extremophilic cell membranes
raw_source_fields.note: Important models for archaeal molecular biology.

raw_source_fields.traits: Thermoacidophilic growth
raw_source_fields.note: Thermoacidophiles found in geothermal areas.

raw_source_fields.traits: Grows at high temperature and low pH
raw_source_fields.note: A model for archaeal chromosomal replication and cellular division.

raw_source_fields.traits: Gametophyte-dominant; spores; no true vascular tissue
raw_source_fields.note: Early land plants helped establish terrestrial habitats, while moss lineages retained a dominant gametophyte.

raw_source_fields.traits: Water-holding cells; peat formation
raw_source_fields.note: Peat mosses influence carbon storage and wetland acidity.

raw_source_fields.traits: Acidifying growth; high water retention
raw_source_fields.note: Sphagnum plants create waterlogged peatlands with slow decomposition.

raw_source_fields.traits: Wetland moss
raw_source_fields.note: Peatland moss distributed across broad temperate areas.

raw_source_fields.traits: Xylem and phloem; lignified support; sporophyte dominance
raw_source_fields.note: Transport and structural tissues enabled taller terrestrial growth and diverse vascular ecologies.

raw_source_fields.traits: Fronds; spores; vascular tissue
raw_source_fields.note: Ferns diversified extensively in humid terrestrial settings and persist globally.

raw_source_fields.traits: Often upright trunks; large fronds
raw_source_fields.note: Tree ferns were conspicuous in many Mesozoic forests.

raw_source_fields.traits: Pollen and ovules; seed development
raw_source_fields.note: Seeds freed reproduction from surface-water dependence and protected embryos.

raw_source_fields.traits: Cones; pollen; wood; many evergreen leaves
raw_source_fields.note: Conifers dominate important high-latitude and montane forests.

raw_source_fields.traits: Needle or scale leaves; naked ovules
raw_source_fields.note: Conifers occupied diverse Mesozoic habitats before flowering plant radiation.

raw_source_fields.traits: Seed-bearing woody plants
raw_source_fields.note: Includes many living conifer families.

raw_source_fields.traits: Resin canals; woody cones
raw_source_fields.note: Includes pines, spruces, firs, and larches.

raw_source_fields.traits: Needles in fascicles in many
raw_source_fields.note: Pines are important fire- and drought-adapted trees.

raw_source_fields.traits: Conifer with needle fascicles
raw_source_fields.note: Widespread Eurasian tree adapted to cool climates.

raw_source_fields.traits: Flowers; enclosed seeds; double fertilization
raw_source_fields.note: Flowering plants radiated during the Cretaceous alongside pollinators and herbivores.

raw_source_fields.traits: Tricolpate pollen in core eudicots
raw_source_fields.note: A large flowering plant lineage; class circumscription differs by system.

raw_source_fields.traits: Diverse flowers and fruits
raw_source_fields.note: An important angiosperm order occupying many habitats.

raw_source_fields.traits: Hypanthium in many; diverse fruits
raw_source_fields.note: Contains roses, apples, pears, cherries, and strawberries.

raw_source_fields.traits: Prickles in many; fragrant flowers
raw_source_fields.note: Wild roses occupy temperate regions worldwide.

raw_source_fields.traits: Pink flowers; vitamin-rich hips
raw_source_fields.note: A wild rose native to Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia.

raw_source_fields.traits: Asci and ascospores; diverse yeast and filament forms
raw_source_fields.note: Ascomycetes include lichens, decomposers, crop pathogens, and baking yeasts.

raw_source_fields.traits: Single-celled budding forms common
raw_source_fields.note: Fermentation made budding yeasts major partners of humans.

raw_source_fields.traits: Many sugar-fermenting yeasts
raw_source_fields.note: This order includes laboratory and industrial yeasts.

raw_source_fields.traits: Fermentative metabolic diversity
raw_source_fields.note: Yeasts adapted to fruit and other sugar-rich environments.

raw_source_fields.traits: Alcoholic fermentation
raw_source_fields.note: Used to study genetics, aging, and basic cell biology.

raw_source_fields.traits: Unicellular eukaryote; budding; fermentation
raw_source_fields.note: A model eukaryote with an extensively studied genome and cell cycle.

raw_source_fields.traits: Basidia bearing sexual spores; mushrooms in many
raw_source_fields.note: Major wood-decaying fungi, mushrooms, rusts and smuts.

raw_source_fields.traits: Complex fruiting bodies in many
raw_source_fields.note: Includes gilled mushrooms, bracket fungi and puffballs.

raw_source_fields.traits: Gills or transformed spore-bearing structures
raw_source_fields.note: Includes edible and poisonous mushrooms.

raw_source_fields.traits: Veils and gill-bearing fruiting bodies in many
raw_source_fields.note: Contains edible cultivated mushrooms and their relatives.

raw_source_fields.traits: Fleshy fruiting bodies; dark mature gills
raw_source_fields.note: Includes the domesticated button mushroom.

raw_source_fields.traits: Often two-spored basidia
raw_source_fields.note: Widely farmed as white button, cremini, and portobello mushrooms.

raw_source_fields.traits: Chlorophyll c; fucoxanthin in many
raw_source_fields.note: Photosynthetic lineages are central to marine food webs and global carbon cycling.

raw_source_fields.traits: Fucoxanthin; multicellularity; alginate walls
raw_source_fields.note: Kelp forests form productive temperate coastal ecosystems.

raw_source_fields.traits: Large blades; holdfasts; underwater canopies
raw_source_fields.note: Kelp forests buffer waves and support diverse marine species.

raw_source_fields.traits: Stipes, blades, and holdfasts
raw_source_fields.note: Giant brown algae in temperate seas.

raw_source_fields.traits: Ribbonlike blades
raw_source_fields.note: Important habitat formers on rocky coasts.

raw_source_fields.traits: Finger-like blade divisions
raw_source_fields.note: Common in rocky North Atlantic coastal zones.

raw_source_fields.count: Tens of thousands of named species
raw_source_fields.traits: Silica frustules; photosynthetic unicells
raw_source_fields.note: Diatoms produce substantial marine and freshwater primary productivity.

raw_source_fields.traits: Cellulose-rich walls in many; diploid dominant; swimming spores
raw_source_fields.note: Oomycetes resemble fungi but are evolutionarily distinct; many are plant pathogens.

raw_source_fields.traits: Plant pathogenicity; zoospores
raw_source_fields.note: Includes organisms responsible for major crop diseases.

raw_source_fields.traits: Oomycete crop pathogen
raw_source_fields.note: A principal cause of devastating potato blights, including the Irish Great Famine.

raw_source_fields.traits: Lobose pseudopodia in many; phagocytosis
raw_source_fields.note: An important eukaryotic lineage, though the taxonomic Protozoa umbrella is not a true clade.

raw_source_fields.traits: Tubular pseudopodia
raw_source_fields.note: Amoebas change shape to feed and migrate.

raw_source_fields.traits: Pseudopods; phagocytosis
raw_source_fields.note: Amoebas have served as classic models for cell motility.

raw_source_fields.traits: Large lobose pseudopodia
raw_source_fields.note: A widely used teaching organism in cell biology.

raw_source_fields.traits: Flagellates; diverse feeding strategies; crystalline rods
raw_source_fields.note: Some members photosynthesize; others are parasites or free-living heterotrophs.

raw_source_fields.traits: Distinct kinetoplast mitochondrial DNA
raw_source_fields.note: Includes disease-causing trypanosomes and free-living relatives.

raw_source_fields.traits: Flagellated protists; complex parasite cycles
raw_source_fields.note: Trypanosomes evolved intricate host-vector life cycles.

raw_source_fields.traits: Variant surface glycoproteins; antigenic variation
raw_source_fields.note: A parasite transmitted by tsetse flies that can cause human African trypanosomiasis.

raw_source_fields.traits: Cilia; nuclear dimorphism in many
raw_source_fields.note: Ciliates have specialized feeding apparatus and dual nuclear systems.

raw_source_fields.traits: Coordinated ciliary currents
raw_source_fields.note: Includes major protist laboratory models.

raw_source_fields.traits: Cilia; contractile vacuoles
raw_source_fields.note: Classic freshwater protists with sophisticated ciliary coordination.

raw_source_fields.traits: Elongated body; oral groove
raw_source_fields.note: A familiar protist viewed in microscope ponds samples.

raw_source_fields.count: 1,796,900 species listed in Catalogue of Life (Sept 2026 XR)
raw_source_fields.traits: Multicellularity; developmental gene networks; extracellular collagen; heterotrophy
raw_source_fields.note: Animals emerged among marine eukaryotes during the Neoproterozoic. Body plans diversified dramatically across the Ediacaran–Cambrian transition; fossil and molecular clocks do not agree on a single origin date.

source_initialization_override.effective_count_text: 1,796,900 species listed in Catalogue of Life (Sept 2026 XR)
source_initialization_override.note: Source uses T.Animalia.parent and T.Animalia.count after initial a(...) creation.

raw_source_fields.traits: Eight rows of ciliary comb plates; prey-capturing colloblasts; diffuse nerve net
raw_source_fields.note: A proposed earliest-diverging animal lineage based on synteny data. Whether it or sponges branch first remains contested; neural origins are consequently debated.

raw_source_fields.traits: Choanocyte filter feeding; porous aquiferous canals; spicules / spongin
raw_source_fields.note: Sponge-like remains may predate the Cambrian, but the oldest fossil assignments are disputed. Most lack organized nerves, muscles and a conventional gut.

raw_source_fields.traits: Flattened ciliated body; very few cell types; no neurons
raw_source_fields.note: Tiny creeping marine animals that illuminate early animal tissue evolution; relationships to cnidarians and bilaterians remain under study.

raw_source_fields.traits: Shared developmental regulators; increasingly complex epithelia
raw_source_fields.note: A proposed group generally including Placozoa, Cnidaria and Bilateria, though some deep relationships remain debated.

raw_source_fields.traits: Cnidocytes with stinging organelles; gastrovascular cavity; radial tendencies
raw_source_fields.note: Cnidarians evolved specialized nerve nets and stinging cells. Many reef builders shaped Paleozoic and later seas.

raw_source_fields.traits: Polyp-only adult; many photosymbioses; reef construction
raw_source_fields.note: Scleractinian corals radiated especially from the Triassic onward after earlier reef systems collapsed.

raw_source_fields.ety: Medusa, Greek mythological name for the jellyfish stage
raw_source_fields.traits: Many life cycles include medusae; specialized sensory structures
raw_source_fields.note: Gelatinous predators evolved diverse pulsating medusae and sessile stages.

raw_source_fields.traits: Anteroposterior polarity; mesoderm; bilateral ancestry
raw_source_fields.note: Bilaterians probably originated in the Ediacaran; many recognizable body plans become abundant in the Cambrian. A number of descendants later evolved radial symmetry.

raw_source_fields.traits: Diverse neural and embryological patterns; ecdysozoan and spiralian branches
raw_source_fields.note: Includes arthropods, mollusks, annelids and many worm phyla. The old “mouth-first” rule has exceptions and does not diagnose every species.

raw_source_fields.traits: Some branches with spiral cleavage; diverse larval forms
raw_source_fields.note: Includes mollusks, annelids and flatworms. Not all spiralians retain spiral cleavage.

raw_source_fields.traits: Mantle; muscular foot (often modified); radula in many groups
raw_source_fields.note: An exceptionally varied Cambrian-origin group; shells fossilize readily, leaving rich records of Paleozoic–Cenozoic oceans.

raw_source_fields.traits: Embryonic torsion; diverse shells or shell loss; aquatic and terrestrial habits
raw_source_fields.note: Gastropods radiated across marine, freshwater and terrestrial environments.

raw_source_fields.traits: Two hinged shells; filter-feeding gills in most; no radula
raw_source_fields.note: Bivalves became major marine filter feeders and expanded ecologically during Mesozoic diversification.

raw_source_fields.traits: Arms/tentacles around head; advanced eyes and behavior; jet propulsion
raw_source_fields.note: Once represented by abundant shelled forms; coleoid cephalopods subsequently diversified high-performance locomotion and nervous systems.

raw_source_fields.ety: Ammon, Egyptian deity depicted with ram horns
raw_source_fields.traits: Chambered coiled shell; complex sutures in many groups
raw_source_fields.note: Ammonoids evolved in the Devonian, recovered after several mass extinctions, and disappeared at the end-Cretaceous extinction.

raw_source_fields.traits: Internalized/reduced shells; chromatophores; complex learning
raw_source_fields.note: Squids, cuttlefish and octopuses evolved rapid camouflage and large centralized brains.

raw_source_fields.traits: Eight sucker-bearing arms; shell highly reduced or absent; dexterity
raw_source_fields.note: Octopuses evolved unusually distributed nervous systems and sophisticated object manipulation.

raw_source_fields.traits: Three hearts; arm-local circuitry; rapid skin-pattern control
raw_source_fields.note: A modern shallow-water octopus complex; some populations historically assigned to this name represent other species.

raw_source_fields.traits: Serially repeated segments; chaetae in many; hydrostatic support
raw_source_fields.note: Marine worms were important Cambrian sediment mixers; earthworms later helped reshape soils.

raw_source_fields.traits: Clitellum for reproduction; direct development common
raw_source_fields.note: A mostly freshwater and terrestrial diversification of annelid worms.

raw_source_fields.traits: Dorsoventrally flat; no coelom; many parasitic taxa
raw_source_fields.note: Includes free-living planarians and multiple independently diverse parasitic lineages.

raw_source_fields.traits: Ecdysis / molting of an external cuticle
raw_source_fields.note: A molecularly supported group uniting arthropods, roundworms, tardigrades and velvet worms.

raw_source_fields.traits: Collagenous molted cuticle; pseudocoelom; longitudinal muscles
raw_source_fields.note: Highly abundant in many soils and sediments; some species are parasitic or key laboratory models.

raw_source_fields.traits: Segmented appendages; molting; distinct limb specializations
raw_source_fields.note: Cambrian lobopodian fossils illuminate the evolution of articulated limbs.

raw_source_fields.traits: Four pairs of lobopod legs; cryptobiosis in many species
raw_source_fields.note: Some tolerate desiccation by entering a tun state; they are not universally resistant to all extremes.

raw_source_fields.traits: Soft lobopod legs; adhesive slime jets; tracheae
raw_source_fields.note: Living velvet worms preserve combinations of features helpful for interpreting Cambrian panarthropods.

raw_source_fields.traits: Jointed appendages; chitinous exoskeleton; segmented body
raw_source_fields.note: Most described animal species are arthropods. Their Cambrian ancestors diversified in seas before insects colonized land and air.

raw_source_fields.traits: Three longitudinal lobes; many mineralized dorsal segments
raw_source_fields.note: Iconic Paleozoic marine arthropods, extinct at the end-Permian extinction. Not direct ancestors of modern insects.

raw_source_fields.traits: Chelicerae feeding appendages; no antennae
raw_source_fields.note: Marine ancestors gave rise to extensive terrestrial arachnid radiations.

raw_source_fields.traits: Four pairs of walking legs in adult typical forms; chelicerae
raw_source_fields.note: Arachnids are major terrestrial predators, parasites and soil inhabitants.

raw_source_fields.traits: Spinnerets producing silk; venomous fangs in most
raw_source_fields.note: Spider silk and aerial prey capture diversified through the Mesozoic.

raw_source_fields.traits: Mandibles derived from modified appendages
raw_source_fields.note: Unites myriapods and pancrustaceans; several deep relationships remain under revision.

raw_source_fields.traits: Many trunk segments; terrestrial life
raw_source_fields.note: Early land arthropods included myriapod relatives adapting to oxygen-rich terrestrial microhabitats.

raw_source_fields.traits: Molecularly supported clade that nests hexapods within crustacean-grade ancestors
raw_source_fields.note: “Crustacea” excluding insects is paraphyletic; this tree keeps insects and other crustaceans together.

raw_source_fields.traits: Characteristically 19 segments; specialized thoracic limbs
raw_source_fields.note: Crabs, lobsters and shrimp have repeatedly occupied strikingly different marine and freshwater niches.

raw_source_fields.traits: Five pairs of thoracic walking limbs
raw_source_fields.note: Decapods became major marine scavengers, predators and ecosystem engineers.

raw_source_fields.traits: Six walking legs on thorax; land adaptations
raw_source_fields.note: Hexapods originated on land and subsequently evolved wings in the insect lineage.

raw_source_fields.traits: Head, thorax and abdomen; three leg pairs; wings in most lineages
raw_source_fields.note: The largest described animal class; winged insects later drove terrestrial pollination and food webs.

raw_source_fields.traits: Larva, pupa and adult; distinct feeding niches
raw_source_fields.note: Complete metamorphosis helped beetles, butterflies, flies and bees partition ecological roles.

raw_source_fields.traits: Protective hardened elytra over hindwings
raw_source_fields.note: Beetles diversified alongside plants, wood decomposers and other ecosystems.

raw_source_fields.traits: Scale-covered wings; coiled proboscis in many adults
raw_source_fields.note: Lepidopteran diversification closely interacted with flowering plants during the Cretaceous and Cenozoic.

raw_source_fields.ety: Danaus, Greek mythic king; plexippus, mythological personal name
raw_source_fields.traits: Toxic milkweed diet; long-distance multigenerational migration
raw_source_fields.note: The North American migratory populations depend on milkweed breeding habitat and overwintering forests.

raw_source_fields.traits: Hook-linked membranous wings in most; parasitoidism and eusociality
raw_source_fields.note: Several eusocial lineages evolved complex division of labor and sophisticated collective behavior.

raw_source_fields.traits: One flying wing pair; balancing halteres
raw_source_fields.note: Dipterans diversified as pollinators, decomposers and some major disease vectors.

raw_source_fields.traits: Includes echinoderms and chordates; multiple embryo-development patterns
raw_source_fields.note: The name refers to an embryological generalization with exceptions; fossil representatives appear by the Cambrian.

raw_source_fields.traits: Water vascular system; calcitic endoskeleton; secondary pentaradial symmetry
raw_source_fields.note: Cambrian stem forms reveal the transition from bilaterian ancestors to characteristic adult radial plans.

raw_source_fields.traits: Tube feet; regenerative arms; usually five rays
raw_source_fields.note: Sea stars evolved diverse predatory feeding strategies in benthic marine habitats.

raw_source_fields.traits: Fused test plates; movable spines; Aristotle’s lantern in most
raw_source_fields.note: Regular echinoids diversified in the Paleozoic; irregular echinoids radiated in Mesozoic seas.

raw_source_fields.traits: Notochord; dorsal hollow nerve cord; pharyngeal openings; postanal tail at some stage
raw_source_fields.note: Cambrian fossils preserve chordate-like and vertebrate-like animals. Tunicates and vertebrates are close relatives.

raw_source_fields.traits: Larval notochord; cellulose-like tunic in adults
raw_source_fields.note: Genomic evidence places tunicates as the living sister lineage to vertebrates.

raw_source_fields.traits: Specialized cranium; vertebral elements in most; neural crest
raw_source_fields.note: Early vertebrates were jawless marine animals; jawed lineages later radiated on reefs and beyond.

raw_source_fields.traits: Cartilage-dominant skeleton; tooth replacement; electroreception in many
raw_source_fields.note: Cartilaginous fish radiated from Paleozoic jawed-vertebrate ancestors.

raw_source_fields.traits: Endochondral bone; lungs or swim bladder ancestrally
raw_source_fields.note: Cladistically includes all tetrapods: humans are deeply nested within bony vertebrates.

raw_source_fields.traits: Fin rays supported by dermal skeleton
raw_source_fields.note: Teleosts underwent a major Mesozoic–Cenozoic diversification in fresh and marine waters.

raw_source_fields.traits: Paired fleshy fins/limbs with internal bones
raw_source_fields.note: The lineages of coelacanths and lungfish diverged from the ancestor that also led to land vertebrates.

raw_source_fields.traits: Digit-bearing limbs ancestrally; air breathing and modified senses
raw_source_fields.note: Originated from Devonian sarcopterygian ancestry; some descendants later lost limbs or returned to water.

raw_source_fields.traits: Permeable skin; often aquatic larval stage; diverse reproduction
raw_source_fields.note: Modern amphibians radiated after early tetrapod lineages, with a fossil record extending into the Paleozoic.

raw_source_fields.traits: Amniotic membranes; reproduction less tied to standing water
raw_source_fields.note: The amniotic egg enabled major diversification on land during the Carboniferous and Permian.

raw_source_fields.traits: Single ancestral lower temporal skull opening
raw_source_fields.note: Includes Permian sail-backed forms, therapsids and living mammals. Many early synapsids are not true mammals.

raw_source_fields.traits: Mammary glands; hair; three middle-ear ossicles
raw_source_fields.note: Crown mammals originated by the Mesozoic and radiated extensively after the K–Pg extinction.

raw_source_fields.traits: Egg laying; milk secretion without nipples
raw_source_fields.note: Surviving egg-laying mammals from an ancient mammalian divergence.

raw_source_fields.traits: Shared reproductive and skeletal traits
raw_source_fields.note: Unites marsupials and placentals; deep lineages diverged in Mesozoic time.

raw_source_fields.traits: Short gestation in many species; prolonged lactation
raw_source_fields.note: Marsupial evolutionary history spans South America, Antarctica and Australia.

raw_source_fields.traits: Extended gestation with complex chorioallantoic placenta
raw_source_fields.note: Major orders diversified before and after the K–Pg boundary; exact divergence dates are debated.

raw_source_fields.traits: Grasping extremities in many; forward-facing eyes in many
raw_source_fields.note: Primates diversified in Paleocene–Eocene forests, with multiple adaptive radiations.

raw_source_fields.traits: Large brains; flexible shoulder; long juvenile dependence
raw_source_fields.note: Orangutans, gorillas, chimpanzees, bonobos and humans are living members of one family.

raw_source_fields.traits: Habitual bipedalism; high behavioral flexibility; stone tools in many fossil contexts
raw_source_fields.note: Homo first appears in the late Pliocene; several lineages coexisted in the Pleistocene.

raw_source_fields.traits: Cumulative culture; symbolic language; extreme ecological flexibility
raw_source_fields.note: Anatomically modern humans have an African fossil record dating to roughly 300,000 years ago.

raw_source_fields.traits: Carnassial dental adaptations, modified in omnivores
raw_source_fields.note: Carnivorans radiated in Paleogene terrestrial ecosystems; pinnipeds returned to the sea.

raw_source_fields.traits: Retractile claws in most; ambush predation; obligate carnivory
raw_source_fields.note: Modern cats include small felines and roaring pantherines.

raw_source_fields.traits: Powerful jaws; roaring anatomy in many
raw_source_fields.note: Genus with lions, tigers, jaguars, leopards and snow leopards; classification of some members changes.
